chunks: Abu Jaʿfar عليه السلام passed by me while I was sitting with the judge in al-Madinah. The next day I went to him, and he said to me: “What was that gathering in which I saw you yesterday?”

He said: I said to him, “May I be your ransom, this judge honors me, so I sometimes sit with him.” He said to me: “And what makes you secure from the curse descending and encompassing you along with him?”

key_terms.الْقَاضِي: the judge; the judicial figure with whom the narrator was sitting
key_terms.جَلَسْتُ: I sat; indicating participation in the gathering
key_terms.فَتَعُمَّكَ: then it encompasses you; meaning it reaches and includes you
key_terms.مُكْرِمٌ: one who shows honor or respect

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام warn against sitting with judges in their gatherings?
ai.summary: This hadith relates Imam Muhammad al-Baqir عليه السلام reproaching Muhammad ibn Muslim for sitting in the gathering of a judge in al-Madinah. It warns that keeping company with unjust or condemned judicial authority can expose a person to divine curse along with them, highlighting caution in social and moral association.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) passed by me while I was sitting with the judge in Madinah.
The next day, I went to him, and Imam (as) said to me: "What was the gathering I saw you in yesterday?"

I said to Him (as): "May I be your ransom! This judge honors me, so I sometimes sit with him."
Imam (as) said to me:
"And what ensures you that the curse will not descend and encompass you along with him?"
